# Evidence status

> The historical pilot and incremental benchmark results have been retired.
> This article intentionally contains no performance numbers until one complete
> `publication-full` study has been acquired and validated. The final narrative,
> tables, and figures must be generated from one immutable study ID.

# Research question

For the same public single-cell expression matrices and deterministic query
workloads, how do the `embedded`, `bpcells`, and `h5` backends trade backend
construction time, stored size, process memory, fresh-process startup, warmed
single-gene latency, and a 12-gene block read as cell count grows?

This is an engineering benchmark, not a comparison of biological methods. It
does not claim controlled cold-disk behaviour, statistical significance,
cross-machine generality, or end-to-end Viewer interaction performance.

# Backends

| | `embedded` | `bpcells` | `h5` |
|---|---|---|---|
| expression location | inside the `.crb` | sibling `.bpcells/` directory | sibling `.h5` file |
| runtime representation | in-memory sparse matrix | lazy BPCells matrix | lazy TENx/HDF5 matrix |
| portability unit | one file | `.crb` plus directory | `.crb` plus HDF5 file |

# Public sources and study grid

The study uses the 10x mouse brain E18 dataset (`GSE93421`, `SRP096558`) and
the CELLxGENE PsychAD HBCC human prefrontal-cortex dataset (DOI
`10.1038/s41597-025-04687-5`). Each acquired file must match its pinned byte
size and SHA-256 value.

| phase | source tiers | backends |
|---|---|---|
| A/B | mouse and human at 50k and 150k cells | embedded, bpcells, h5 |
| C1 | mouse 400k and human 300k | embedded, bpcells, h5 |
| C2 | both complete sources | bpcells, h5 |

Every tier has three independent build processes and two independent access
processes per build. Backend order rotates across builds. Complete-source
`embedded` results are labelled `not representable` because both matrices
exceed `dgCMatrix`'s 32-bit non-zero index limit.

# Measurement and correctness

A deterministic 12-gene query plan is prepared and frozen in a separate process
before any timed backend build. Preparation cost is reported separately. Every
build and access process must reproduce the same query-plan fingerprint. The
exact gene order, roles, densities, and reference fingerprints are retained in
`query_panel.csv`.

The first getter call is a fresh-process first query, not a cold-disk query.
Subsequent genes are warmed and measured in deterministic passes. Correctness
fingerprints for the first row and full 12-gene block are checked outside the
timed expressions; any mismatch invalidates the study.

The independent process is the experimental unit. Final tables report raw rows,
median, observed range, and process `n`, plus matched backend ratios within the
same source, tier, phase, and metric. No significance test is performed.

# Publication gate

A final report is generated only when A/B, C1, and C2 share one study ID, clean
acquisition Git SHA, source hashes, CPU, OS, R platform, key dependency versions,
thread count, and storage description. All phases and derived outputs are frozen
inside one immutable result bundle; its `CURRENT` pointer changes last.

The combined evidence will be read from:

```text
tests/bench/result/publication-full/
├── CURRENT
└── runs/<study-id>/
    ├── phases/{ab,c1,c2}/
    ├── combined_metrics.csv
    ├── backend_ratios.csv
    ├── correctness.csv
    ├── query_plan_metrics.csv
    ├── query_panel.csv
    ├── source_provenance.csv
    ├── summary.md
    └── figures/expression_backend_benchmark_publication_full.png
```

# Reproduction

Run from a clean checkout in the pinned environment on an exclusive node with
local scratch storage:

```bash
BENCH_THREADS=1 \
  BENCH_SOURCE_CACHE=/persistent/cache \
  BENCH_SCRATCH_PARENT=/local/scratch \
  BENCH_STORAGE_DESCRIPTION="local NVMe; ext4; model=<model>" \
  tests/bench/run_publication_full.sh
```

After the immutable study is returned, this article should be completed from
its generated `summary.md`, CSV tables, raw process rows, and combined figure.
The full protocol and interpretation limits are documented in
`tests/bench/METHODOLOGY.md`.
